log: IS BUFFERING PREDICTABLE FROM REDUNDANCY STRUCTURE -- engineering or theory
Five results measured the same thing: mechanism is right locally and does not reach the
far field. loop_slack measured why -- only 11.7% of knockouts cost >1% of growth. Cells
buffer. If that buffering is predictable from redundancy STRUCTURE, the composition gap is
engineering. If not, it is theory and no data collection closes it.

BUFFERING IS PREDICTABLE AND USABLE. Structure separates buffered from not-buffered out
of sample at 0.6963, and using it raises the model's own precision from
0.7658 to 0.8228 against a shuffled 95th of 0.7785. That is the first
time in this project that naming a missing layer also let us USE it -- loop_recall named
one and made the predictor worse.
BUT IT IS NOT REDUNDANCY, AND THAT WAS THE HYPOTHESIS. All four redundancy features
point the WRONG WAY: more isozymes predicts NOT buffered (0.3325),
and more sole-catalyst reactions predicts buffered (0.6413) -- both
the reverse of 'something else covers the job'. What actually separates them is
CENTRALITY: buffered genes have fewer interactions (0.2602), sit outside
complexes (0.3689) and are lowly expressed (0.3647).
So the model is not being defeated by biological back-up. It is over-calling
PERIPHERAL genes -- ones carrying unique chemistry in parts of the network the cell
does not lean on. That is a model-scope problem, which is engineering, and it is a
different problem from the one the buffering story predicted.
